title: The longest night
premise: On the longest night of the year, snow comes to the edge of the table. Wick goes down to the store and gets lost in the snow, and Pip leaves Thimble with the light to bring the old keeper home.

scenes.summary: The lamp glass frosts over on the longest night

problem.summary: The lamp's glass has frosted over in the cold

actions.text: On the longest night of the year, the snow came all the way to the edge of the table.
Snow! It's snowing on the Reader too! Look!
I've never seen snow from dry land before!
I've wound Grandmother's thread back on its spool. Every inch of it.
The last time I was this cold, somebody threw me a rope.
The last time I was this cold, I crossed a ladder to get home.
Longest night of the year. I'll fetch the oil up from the store, same as every night.
I'll go! You can't see the steps in the...
Forty winters I've walked those steps, lad. I don't need eyes for them.
And down he went, one paw on the wall, counting every step.
The glass is frosting over! The light can't get out!
And Wick will need it to find his way back!
Have you got anything to wipe it clear?
That's it! Rub, rub, rub...
There! Shine all the way down the steps!

actions.outcome: the Reader's gift wiped the glass clear

actions.text: Thank you! But that won't wipe the frost.
Something soft, maybe? Something warm?
Thimble had polished a great many thimbles in her time. She knew exactly what to do.
A bit of elbow grease, and... there!
The lamp shone. The snow fell. And the old keeper didn't come back.
He's been gone too long. Much too long.
Go and find him, Pip. I'll keep the light till you're back.
But a keeper never leaves the light.
Then I'll be the keeper for a bit. I know what this light means to someone lost.
Will you come with me? Into the snow?
So down went the little fox, a hundred and twelve steps, into the longest night.

scenes.summary: Wick is lost in the snow, and his logbook is out in the Reader's room

problem.summary: Wick's logbook lies half buried in the snow at the foot of the steps

actions.text: At the bottom of the steps, the snow had covered everything. The path, the rocks, and every footprint.
Wick? Wick! Where are you?
His footprints just stop. The snow's filled them in.
Then something glinted, half buried in the snow at the foot of the steps.
There, in the snow! Can you reach it for me?
Wick's logbook! He never goes anywhere without it.

actions.outcome: the Reader brought the logbook back from the room

actions.text: Thank you. But it's the shiny thing I need, there in the snow.
So the little fox dug it out of the snow himself.
Wick's logbook! He never goes anywhere without it.

actions.outcome: Pip dug the logbook out of the snow

actions.text: He's lost. Wick's lost, out in the snow.
Every lost thing follows the light home. But how can he follow it, if he can't see it?
Then the light will just have to be bigger than the dark. Moth?
And up went the little light, high above the snow.
The kite from the night Thimble came! Can I borrow it again?
And up went the little light, high above the snow.
The ladder from the night Thimble came! Can I borrow it again?
And up went the little light, high above the snow.
Wick! Wick! Follow the light!

scenes.summary: Wick can't see where the edge of the gap is in the snow

problem.summary: Wick can't see where the edge of the gap is in the snow

actions.text: Pip? Is that your light, lad? Brightest little light I ever saw.
The old keeper stood at the edge of the gap, with the snow coming down, and no way to tell where the ground stopped.
Forty winters on this shore, and tonight I can't find my own way home.
I got over this gap once, with help. Can you help me get him across?
Hold still, Wick. And catch!
Hmph. Now where did you learn that?
One rung at a time, Wick. I've got you.
Don't look down, eh? Easy for some.
A kite? At my age?
Oh. Oh my. Hmph. Rather nice, actually.

actions.outcome: Wick flew over on a kite

actions.text: I don't think that'll get him over.
Something long, maybe? Something to hold on to?
Then Pip saw it. Wick's own rope, right where he'd left it, the night the light went out.
Hold still, Wick. And catch!
Hmph. Now where did you learn that?

actions.outcome: Pip threw Wick's own rope across

actions.text: Hmph. Not bad, keeper. Not bad at all.
You dropped this. It was in the snow at the bottom of the steps.
Forty years of lost things coming home, all in here.
You brought us all home tonight, lad. Time you kept the lamp.
The lamp, and the log, and all of it. They're yours, keeper.
Mine? But who'll grumble at me?
I'll grumble from my comfy chair. Loudly.
And just then, the snow stopped, the clouds opened, and the whole sky came out.
I don't need eyes for the stars, lad. I know them all by heart.
There's the Lantern. Every keeper's first star.
And the Kite, with her long tail.
And that one? It looks like a fox.
Don't know that one. Must be new.
They say every keeper gets a star. Looks like that one's yours.
A shooting star! Quick, make a wish!
They climbed the hundred and twelve steps together. And the old keeper didn't count them once.
Welcome home, keepers. I kept her shining, every minute.
And when the stars had faded, and the morning came over the edge of the table...
...the new keeper put out the lamp himself, for the very first time. And the old keeper fell asleep in his comfy chair.
And whatever the Reader gave that night, the book kept safe, for another time.
Because lost things, as you'll find, have a way of coming back.
The snow fell, soft as a held breath.
Up at the top, a small mouse kept the great lamp turning.
Somewhere out in the white, an old badger counted his steps.
